questions.text: Which of the below is NOT correct when it comes to the definition of an API?

choices.text: An API stands for Application Programming Interface
Serves as an intermediary
Acts as the connection between systems
Defines how different software components or systems can interact with each other
Outlines the methods and protocols through which one system can communicate with another

questions.reference_answer: An API stands for Application Programming Interface. It defines how different software components or systems can interact with each other.

questions.text: Which of the below is NOT correct when it comes to the definition of REST?

choices.text: REST stands for Representational State Transfer
It is an architectural style for designing networked applications
RESTful APIs are built based on the principles of REST
Outlines the methods and protocols through which one system can communicate with another

questions.text: What does the 'Representational' part of REST stands for?

choices.text: Representing the state of the program
Representing the state of the Python data we return
Representing the Python data in a specific format (can be json, xml, etc.) when we return it
Representing the API`s main functions

questions.text: How do we transfer the data when using REST?

choices.text: Using HTTP requests
Using APIs
Using json
All of the above

questions.text: What is the difference between MPA (Multi-Page Application) and SPA(Single-Page Application)?

choices.text: An MPA uses only JavaScript for rendering content, whereas an SPA does not use JavaScript at all.
An MPA can only connect to one database, while an SPA can connect to multiple databases at the same time.
An MPA reloads the entire page from the server for each new request or navigation, while an SPA loads a single HTML page and dynamically updates content in the browser without full page reloads.
An MPA is designed only for mobile devices, while an SPA is designed only for desktop browsers.

questions.text: Which of the following is part of the key principles of  RESTful APIs?

choices.text: RESTful APIs follow a client-server architecture - the client sends requests to the server, and the server processes those requests and sends back responses

RESTful APIs are stateless - each request from a client to the server must contain all the necessary information to understand and process the request. The server does not store any client state between requests
RESTful APIs have a uniform interface - This includes using standard HTTP methods to perform actions on resources and using standard HTTP status codes to indicate the outcome of a request
In RESTful APIs, everything is treated as a resource, which can be accessed and manipulated using standard HTTP methods
Resources in RESTful APIs are represented in different formats
All answers are correct
